input: Audit and update all my online account passwords

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The user says 'all' accounts — knowing whether this means every account ever created vs. only active/important ones drastically changes the scale and effort of the task.
Are these purely personal accounts, or do work/shared/family accounts need to be included? This affects permissions, coordination with others, and sensitivity.
The user may have a deadline (e.g., after a breach) or a time budget per session, which determines how the task should be broken into chunks.
Whether the user is already using a password manager (or is open to one) completely changes the recommended workflow and tooling.
Knowing what triggered this audit (a suspected breach, routine hygiene, a specific compromised account) determines urgency and where to start.
What 'done well' means varies — it could be unique strong passwords only, or it could also require enabling two-factor authentication on all accounts.
The user may have strong feelings about password rules (length, complexity, passphrases vs. random strings) or privacy concerns about certain tools.

gold.taskTitle: Audit and update all online account passwords
gold.taskDescription: Review every online account the user has, assess the strength and security of each password, and update them to meet a stronger standard.

questions.title: Which accounts are in scope — all ever created, or active ones only?
questions.description: Determine whether the audit covers every account the user has ever registered, or only accounts they actively use today.

questions.title: Are these personal accounts, work accounts, or both?
questions.description: Establish whether the task involves only personal accounts or also includes professional, shared, or family accounts.

questions.title: What prompted this audit right now?
questions.description: Understand the trigger — a suspected breach, a news event, routine maintenance — to gauge urgency and set the starting point.

questions.title: Do you have a deadline or time limit for completing this?
questions.description: Find out if there is a hard deadline or a preferred number of hours per sitting, so the task can be structured into manageable sessions.

questions.title: Are you already using a password manager?
questions.description: Determine the user's current tooling so the plan can build on existing habits or recommend and incorporate a password manager from scratch.

questions.title: Should the audit also cover enabling two-factor authentication?
questions.description: Clarify whether 'done well' means strong unique passwords only, or whether two-factor authentication setup is also part of the desired outcome.

questions.title: Do you have a preferred password style — passphrase, random string, or other?
questions.description: Understand the user's preferences around password format, length, or any constraints they want applied when generating new passwords.
